slides.title: Thinking, Feelings, and Imagination
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 3 English, Unit 9: Thinking, Feelings, and Imagination. This last unit of Year 3 explores the world inside your head: thinking, feeling and imagining. You will learn sixteen words for ideas and emotions, including idea, sense, reason, sadness and experience. You will practise imagining, making a choice, giving a reason with because, and suggesting ideas kindly in a group. In the story The Box of Ideas, children at a school by the sea fill a special box with their dreams and hopes. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Use abstract nouns like idea, reason, experience, and sadness to talk about thoughts and feelings.
Say what you imagine and describe the pictures in your mind.
Give a reason for something using because.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to use abstract nouns like idea, reason, experience, and sadness to talk about thoughts and feelings. You will also say what you imagine and describe the pictures in your mind. You will also give a reason for something using because. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: idea, imagine, reason, purpose, choice, sense. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: The Box of Ideas at School
Feelings Are Not Bad or Good
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The Box of Ideas at School and Feelings Are Not Bad or Good. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Abstract Nouns
bullets: An abstract noun names something you cannot see, touch, or hold, such as a feeling, a quality, or an idea. Words like idea, experience, sadness and...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Abstract Nouns. An abstract noun names something you cannot see, touch, or hold, such as a feeling, a quality, or an idea. Words like idea, experience, sadness and kindness are all abstract nouns. They let you talk about what is happening inside your mind and heart. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1 — My Idea for the Box
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Share an Idea. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use AI English for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
